# Bazaar Commerce

> An open-source multi-vendor marketplace engine for cash-on-delivery markets,
> built on MedusaJS 2.18 and Mercur 2.3 in TypeScript. It supplies the money and
> operations layer that stock ecommerce software omits: a double-entry
> settlement ledger keyed on courier remittance rather than payment capture, an
> anti-RTO order confirmation gate, an encrypted digital code vault with a fraud
> gate, and a payout rail for markets Stripe Connect does not serve.

Licence: Apache-2.0. Maintained by Cubitrek (https://cubitrek.com).
Repository: https://github.com/Cubitrek/bazaar-commerce

## Why it exists

In Pakistan, Bangladesh, Egypt, Nigeria and much of South and Southeast Asia
roughly 95% of ecommerce orders are cash on delivery. A courier collects the
money days after the order, remits it in a batch, sometimes short. Between 20%
and 40% of parcels are returned to origin undelivered, and the seller pays
freight both ways. Software that assumes "authorize, capture, then pay the
seller" cannot model any of that.

## Core capabilities

- [COD settlement ledger](https://github.com/Cubitrek/bazaar-commerce/blob/main/docs/cod-settlement.md): double-entry accounting where orders become payable only when a courier remits; ingests remittance files, matches on airway bill, routes short payments and unknown AWBs to an exception queue; handles provincial sales tax on commission and income-tax withholding.
- [Order confirmation before dispatch](https://github.com/Cubitrek/bazaar-commerce/blob/main/docs/order-confirmation.md): holds a parcel until the buyer confirms, over WhatsApp with SMS fallback; risk-scored so most orders are not delayed; silence is treated as consent except in the high-risk band.
- [Digital fulfilment](https://github.com/Cubitrek/bazaar-commerce/blob/main/docs/digital-fulfilment.md): AES-256-GCM encrypted code vault, atomic allocation via FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED so no code reaches two buyers, and a fraud gate that holds on doubt because a released code cannot be recalled.
- Payout provider: pluggable implementation of Mercur's IPayoutProvider for markets where Stripe Connect is unavailable.
- Phone-first OTP authentication with rate limiting, hashed codes and timing-safe comparison.
- Multi-vendor carts: one cart splits into one order per seller, each with its own commission and settlement.

## Technology

TypeScript, MedusaJS 2.18, Mercur 2.3, PostgreSQL, Redis, Next.js, React Native
(Expo), Docker. Package manager: bun. Node 20+.

## Status

Pre-production. The engine has 229 test assertions across seven suites, each
proven able to fail before being trusted. 226 pass on a clean database; three
checks in the CSV suite are order-dependent and documented as an open issue. The
commercial integrations are not contracted: payouts run against a mock driver,
SMS and WhatsApp print to the console, and courier remittance formats are
modelled from documented specifications rather than live files.
